topic: Memory Hierarchy and Caching Strategies: CPU-Storage
explanation: Modern computer systems employ a memory hierarchy to bridge the speed gap between CPU and storage.  This hierarchy consists of multiple levels of memory with varying speeds and capacities.  Caching is a crucial strategy within this hierarchy, exploiting locality of reference (temporal and spatial) to store frequently accessed data in faster memory levels (caches) closer to the CPU, improving performance significantly.  Understanding the memory hierarchy and how caching works is essential for writing efficient programs and designing high-performance systems.
